newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha firm on crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha firm on crude gains.

text.p: Asia naphtha prices firmed driven by crude strength despite weake fundamentals and mogas was stable with sentiment still bearish, traders said on Tuesday.
Rumours were heard that a U.S major sold a mid-June naphtha cargo at between 60 cents to a $1.00 per barrel premia over Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.

Despite the high premium the major received, traders said the market was still under pressure, especially for prompt cargoes. They assessed current premia for these cargoes at between flat to 40 cents.
"The prompt market has ample unsold supplies but once these supplies are absorbed the market should be on its way up," a western trader said.
He said the arbitrage window from the West is now closed, limiting potential supplies coming East.
Another trader said the market should recover in one month time as prices for cargoes loading in the second half of August have firmed.

In the open-specification market, a previous contango market for second half July and first half August has narrowed to flat. Traders said that this indicates that the market has firmed for the forward months.
End users in Japan and South Korea have already started to buy up their July requirements, said a South Korean trader.
In the naphtha swaps market, both June and July jumped 50 cents to $21.70/$21.80. But the gains were more crude led, traders said.

India was seen gushing out naphtha for May and June loading, traders said. India has tendered to sell up to 165,000 tonnes of naphtha and LNG for May and June loading. They said this may dampen any projected price rise.
Near market close a 97-octane cargo was bid at $24.95, slightly lower from a offer seen on Monday at $25.20. A 92-octane was offered at $23.70 for June loading.
Taiwan has also issued a tender to buy 95-octane unleaded reformate for late June or early July loading. Traders said this would helped support prices in a current bearish market.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
